sections.body: The frozen validation decision retains the Phase 1 baseline: no primary reclaim policy qualified. Later assessment and replication were read after that decision; no rule was retuned. Passive limits and every prespecified protected-boundary replacement remain exploratory. Prior baseline exposure means these chronological partitions are not pristine holdouts.

sections.body: Paired tables use the original-breakout year, session and side (upper-first/lower-first); known no fill contributes a zero alternative outcome only when its path is known. Family common masks exclude missing pairs; individual-mask sensitivity is separately labeled. Candidate performance tables use actual candidate-fill New York year/session and long/short direction, and closed statistics exclude censored fills. No-fill episodes have no invented candidate entry session. A chronological policy may enter after the baseline exited; those opportunity costs remain in the paired comparison.

sections.body: Intervals are saved block-resampling outputs with prespecified block-length sensitivity. Primary-family adjusted intervals are marginal contrasts within each reported cohort; they do not provide simultaneous coverage across all year/session/side cohorts. Protected adjusted intervals apply only to the upper-first prespecified family; mirror and combined views are unadjusted exploratory evidence. Empty cohorts and undefined profit factors/rates remain unavailable. The most recent calendar year is partial. Costs are frozen assumptions, not broker fees. Fixed broker time and New York reporting time differ. Missing minutes, stale source stretches, estimated intrabar order and contract transitions limit exact execution inference. Native TradingView equivalence is unverified. Phase 3 and H10 remain uncomputed.
